holdReason: scripts/validate-knowledge-base.js applies the citation-purity threshold PER SUGGESTION: any suggestion whose unverified ratio exceeds 0.3 must be forced to draft, and a suggestion whose only citation is unverified is immediately quarantined. Because sourceReferences is capped at three, one unverified reference is already 33 percent, so NO unverified reference can enter a published mapping at all. schizophrenia.json is published and carries one qualified-human-verified edge (rank 1 to diabetes-mellitus-type-2, PMID 39324122); flipping the file to draft:true would unpublish that edge, exclude the identity from runtime output, and break the 140/673 published/draft pin, so that path is closed. All three of this edge's PMIDs are pending-verification (registered nowhere or reserved without registration), so the edge cannot enter the knowledge base until a qualified human verifies its citations under docs/citation-verification-sop.md. Mapping approval is not citation verification. This is the batch-89 precedent applied unchanged.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Chronic antipsychotic exposure in the treatment of schizophrenia is associated with tardive dyskinesia and the wider tardive-syndrome burden at quantified rates across a ten-year treated follow-up cohort, a national schizophrenia cohort and a multi-state Medicaid claims population: the 2023 ten-year retrospective follow-up of 123 continuously antipsychotic-treated patients in a Taiwan medical centre (92 completing follow-up) reports that 39 of 92 (42.4 percent) had at least one tardive syndrome episode, that tardive dyskinesia was the most prevalent subtype at 51.3 percent, that a history of extrapyramidal symptoms was a significant risk factor, and that the ten-year remission rate was 74.3 percent (70 percent for tardive dyskinesia against 87.5 percent for tardive dystonia, remission defined as a Visual Analogue Scale score of at most 3) (PMID 37424417); the 2019 French national FACE-SZ cohort of 674 community-dwelling patients with schizophrenia reports extrapyramidal side effects measured on the Simpson-Angus and Abnormal Involuntary Movement scales, with drug-induced parkinsonism at 13.2 percent and tardive dyskinesia at 8.3 percent, and first-generation antipsychotic prescription an adjusted odds ratio of 2.038 (p = 0.047) for DRUG-INDUCED PARKINSONISM (PMID 30695288); and the 2025 descriptive study of 2016-2020 multi-state Medicaid claims following patients with schizophrenia for 12 months after second-generation antipsychotic initiation reports claims-based extrapyramidal-symptom evidence in 13.6 percent (2,288 patients), a mean time to first evidence of 103.7 days, 71.5 percent of first evidence arriving as a medication claim rather than a diagnostic claim, 25.3 percent carrying an extrapyramidal-medication claim on the very date of antipsychotic initiation (prophylactic prescribing), and fewer than 2 percent receiving tardive-dyskinesia-specific VMAT2 inhibitors (PMID 39240484). The registered claim is treatment-mediated association only: the exposure in all three anchors is the prescribed antipsychotic rather than the schizophrenia itself, the FACE-SZ generation gradient points at the agent rather than the diagnosis, and the claims anchor measures extrapyramidal evidence broadly rather than tardive dyskinesia specifically, which its benztropine-dominated medication pattern shows.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of tardive dyskinesia is established for any individual: the exposure in all three anchors is prescribed antipsychotic medication rather than the schizophrenia itself, no anchor includes an antipsychotic-free schizophrenia control arm, and schizophrenia is itself associated with spontaneous orofacial dyskinesia so illness and medication effects cannot be separated within these designs; the ten-year follow-up anchor is retrospective and single-centre with 31 of 123 patients lost to follow-up, defines remission on a Visual Analogue Scale score rather than on examination, and reports antioxidant use associated with remission, which is confounded by indication; the FACE-SZ anchor is cross-sectional, reports its first-generation antipsychotic gradient (adjusted odds ratio 2.038, p = 0.047) for DRUG-INDUCED PARKINSONISM and not for tardive dyskinesia, and its 8.3 percent tardive dyskinesia figure is a point prevalence on the Abnormal Involuntary Movement Scale rather than an incidence; and the Medicaid anchor is claims-based, cannot distinguish tardive dyskinesia from other extrapyramidal syndromes (71.5 percent of first evidence is a benztropine claim and fewer than 2 percent of those with medication claims received tardive-dyskinesia-specific VMAT2 inhibitors), and carries an AUTHOR-INDUSTRY CONFLICT OF INTEREST, two authors being employees of and the research funded by Cerevel Therapeutics. Individual claims require a dated antipsychotic start, stop, dose, formulation and route timeline with dated Abnormal Involuntary Movement Scale examinations before and after initiation, a documented antipsychotic-free interval where one exists, and exclusion of spontaneous orofacial dyskinesia, of other dopamine-blocking agents including metoclopramide and prochlorperazine, of withdrawal-emergent dyskinesia, and of Huntington disease, Wilson disease, stroke and other structural or degenerative movement disorders.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Chronic dopamine D2 receptor blockade in the nigrostriatal pathway is held to produce receptor supersensitivity and altered striatal output that manifests as the choreoathetoid movements of tardive dyskinesia, which is the route the ten-year cohort's episode and remission data quantify in treated patients and the route the FACE-SZ first-generation gradient is consistent with; but whether the prescription produced any individual's tardive dyskinesia independently of the illness, of prior exposure, of metabolic burden and of spontaneous movement disorder remains hypothesized until the movement-disorder findings are read against the medication timeline.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at ten-year-treated-follow-up, national-schizophrenia-cohort and claims-descriptive class, at PHARMACOLOGICAL_IATROGENIC with the antipsychotic prescription named as the proximate agent: the ten-year follow-up anchor is registered first because it is the only anchor reporting course (42.4 percent episode rate, 74.3 percent ten-year remission, tardive dyskinesia the most prevalent subtype at 51.3 percent); the FACE-SZ anchor is registered second because it is the only anchor measuring tardive dyskinesia on the Abnormal Involuntary Movement Scale in a national schizophrenia cohort; and the Medicaid claims anchor is registered third with its endpoint limitation declared on the edge, because it establishes the early extrapyramidal burden after antipsychotic initiation in a large claims population but cannot separate tardive dyskinesia from other extrapyramidal syndromes and carries an author-industry conflict of interest; THE EDGE IS HELD, NOT REGISTERED, in batch 90 because data/knowledge-base/schizophrenia.json is published and the per-suggestion citation-purity gate admits no verified:false reference into it, so this edge and its references are preserved verbatim here pending qualified-human citation verification, and this rationale travels with the edge unchanged when it lands.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: NO ANCHOR IS ANTIPSYCHOTIC-FREE AND NO ANCHOR SEPARATES ILLNESS FROM MEDICATION, since schizophrenia itself is associated with spontaneous orofacial dyskinesia and no located design includes an antipsychotic-free schizophrenia control arm; the course anchor is retrospective and single-centre with 31 of 123 patients lost to follow-up, defines remission as a Visual Analogue Scale score of at most 3 rather than by examination, and reports antioxidant use associated with remission, a confounded comparison; the national cohort anchor is cross-sectional, so its 8.3 percent tardive dyskinesia figure is a point prevalence rather than an incidence, and its adjusted odds ratio of 2.038 for first-generation antipsychotic prescription applies to DRUG-INDUCED PARKINSONISM and NOT to tardive dyskinesia, so it may not be cited as a tardive-dyskinesia risk gradient; the claims anchor measures extrapyramidal evidence broadly (13.6 percent within 12 months, 71.5 percent arriving first as a benztropine claim, fewer than 2 percent on tardive-dyskinesia-specific VMAT2 inhibitors) and cannot identify tardive dyskinesia cases at all, and its prophylactic-prescribing finding (25.3 percent with an extrapyramidal-medication claim on the day of antipsychotic initiation) shows prescribing practice contaminating the endpoint; the claims anchor additionally carries an author-industry conflict of interest (Cerevel Therapeutics employees and funding).
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Spontaneous orofacial dyskinesia associated with schizophrenia itself, which no located anchor separates from drug-induced tardive dyskinesia
Prior antipsychotic exposure predating the recorded timeline, since exposure history is the dominant gradient in the located tardive-dyskinesia literature
Other dopamine-blocking agents outside the recorded psychiatric timeline, including the antiemetics metoclopramide and prochlorperazine
Withdrawal-emergent dyskinesia following dose reduction or cessation rather than dyskinesia produced during exposure
Degenerative and structural movement disorders including Huntington disease, Wilson disease and stroke, and metabolic burden including diabetes

heldEdges.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because it is the primary route the tardive-dyskinesia identity was created to hold: batch 80 refused it only because the identity did not exist and preserved its evidence, batch 88 reserved further evidence against it, and the identity was added to the catalog on 2026-09-28 as the versioned 814th entry precisely so this route could be authored; the located evidence quantifies both burden and course in antipsychotic-treated populations, with 42.4 percent experiencing at least one tardive syndrome episode over ten years and 8.3 percent point prevalence measured on the Abnormal Involuntary Movement Scale in a national schizophrenia cohort; the conservative framing names the antipsychotic prescription as proximate, carries the claims-endpoint limitation, the parkinsonism-versus-tardive-dyskinesia gradient distinction, the attrition and remission-definition limits and the author-industry conflict openly, and requires a dated antipsychotic timeline with dated movement-disorder examinations and exclusion of spontaneous dyskinesia before any individual attribution. THE EDGE LANDS VERBATIM when a qualified human verifies its citations under docs/citation-verification-sop.md; until then it is held rather than registered because the citation-purity gate admits no unverified reference into a published mapping.

sourceReferences.citation: Chou PC, Lee Y, Chang YY, Lin PY, Wang LJ. The Outcome of Antipsychotics-induced Tardive Syndromes: A Ten-year Follow-up Study. Clin Psychopharmacol Neurosci. 2023 Aug 31;21(3):488-498. doi: 10.9758/cpn.22.1000. PMID 37424417.
sourceReferences.note: Retrospective ten-year follow-up of 123 continuously antipsychotic-treated patients in a Taiwan medical centre (92 completing follow-up), registered as this edge's PRIMARY anchor for course: 39 of 92 (42.4 percent) had at least one tardive syndrome episode, tardive dyskinesia was the most prevalent subtype (51.3 percent), a history of extrapyramidal symptoms was a significant risk factor, and the ten-year remission rate was 74.3 percent (tardive dyskinesia 70 percent, tardive dystonia 87.5 percent, remission defined as a Visual Analogue Scale score of at most 3). LIMITATIONS CARRIED: retrospective single-centre design, 31 of 123 lost to follow-up, and antioxidant use reported as associated with remission, a confounded comparison.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: Clin Psychopharmacol Neurosci. 2023;21(3):488-498. Retrospective cohort, 123 patients on continuous antipsychotics at a Taiwan medical centre April 2011 to May 2021, 92 completing 10-year follow-up; abstract states 39 of 92 (42.4%) with at least one tardive syndrome episode, TD the most prevalent subtype (51.3%), concurrent physical illness and history of extrapyramidal symptoms as significant risk factors, remission rate 74.3% over 10 years (tardive dystonia 87.5% versus TD 70%), remission defined as Visual Analogue Scale score <= 3, and antioxidant use (vitamin B6, piracetam) related to remission.
